name: Bashshar ibn Burd
bio: Bashshar ibn Burd, known as Abu Mu'adh, was a blind poet who grew up in Basra. His family came from Tukharistan in Central Asia, and he was a client of the Arab tribe of Uqayl. His career stretched from the last Umayyads into the Abbasid period and took him to Baghdad. He wrote tribal and court praise, satire and love poetry, and al-Jahiz also knew him as an orator and letter writer. Accused of heresy, he was flogged to death and buried in Basra in 167 AH (784 CE) according to al-Zirikli.
